correctness.rationale: The proof uses the exact two-round criterion for burning and exhausts both possible source types in \(T(G)\). For a vertex-node \(v\), the nonneighbor count is \((n-1-d_G(v))+(m-d_G(v))\), which forces a universal center and at most one leaf-edge after the connectivity obstruction is removed. For an edge-node, the \(n-2\) nonincident vertex-nodes force \(n\le3\). Sufficiency is immediate from a center vertex-node with zero or one nonneighbor. A Graph Atlas check through seven vertices found no counterexample and was not used as proof.
